record.paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For all counterexamples to maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), must the counterexample channels have non-negative completely bounded (CB) entropy and/or zero coherent information?

evidence.quote: In the case of Winter’s examples [51] for p >2, one can show that the so-called CB entropy [14] is positive and the coherent information is negative.
Problem 21. Do all counter-examples to multiplicativity (24) have non-negative CB entropy and/or zero coherent information?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ denote the bounded operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, and let a quantum channel be a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) linear map $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$. For $p\geq 1$ define the maximal output $p$-norm
$$\nu_p(\Phi)\;=\;\sup_{\rho}\,\bigl\|\Phi(\rho)\bigr\|_p,$$
where the supremum runs over density operators $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\|X\|_p=(\mathrm{Tr}|X|^p)^{1/p}$. Say that a pair of channels $(\Phi,\Omega)$ is a $p$-multiplicativity counterexample if
$$\nu_p(\Phi\otimes\Omega)\;>\;\nu_p(\Phi)\,\nu_p(\Omega).$$

For a channel $\Phi$ with Stinespring isometry $V:\mathcal{H}_A\to\mathcal{H}_B\otimes\mathcal{H}_E$ such that $\Phi(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}_E(V\rho V^*)$, define the complementary channel $\Phi^c(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}_B(V\rho V^*)$. The completely bounded (CB) entropy of $\Phi$ is
$$S_{CB}(\Phi)\;=\;\inf_{\rho_{RA}}\Bigl[S\bigl((\mathrm{id}_R\otimes\Phi)(\rho_{RA})\bigr)-S(\rho_R)\Bigr],$$
taken over all bipartite states $\rho_{RA}$, where $S(\sigma)=-\mathrm{Tr}(\sigma\log\sigma)$. The coherent information of $\Phi$ at input $\rho$ is
$$I_c(\rho,\Phi)\;=\;S(\Phi(\rho))-S(\Phi^c(\rho)),$$
and $I_c(\Phi)=\sup_\rho I_c(\rho,\Phi)$.

Question: Is it true that for every $p>1$ and every $p$-multiplicativity counterexample $(\Phi,\Omega)$, at least one of the channels $\Phi$, $\Omega$ must have non-negative CB entropy, or have zero coherent information? Equivalently, can a counterexample to multiplicativity exist in which both channels simultaneously have negative CB entropy and non-zero coherent information?
artifact.status_search_result: The maximal $p$-norm multiplicativity conjecture has been disproved for all $p>1$ (Hayden–Winter 2008, and earlier Werner–Holevo for large $p$), and the additivity of minimum output entropy was disproved by Hastings (2009). However, no source surveyed addresses the specific structural question of whether all such counterexample channels must have non-negative CB entropy or zero coherent information. The status appears to be unknown/unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Counterexamples to the Maximal p-Norm Multiplicativity Conjecture for all p > 1
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples to multiplicativity for all p>1 are constructed using random subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples to multiplicativity exist for all p>1, but the specific entropic structural question is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Superadditivity of communication capacity using entangled inputs
status_evidence.snippet: Hastings's counterexample to additivity of minimum output entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples are known but their CB-entropy/coherent-information signatures are not characterized.
